rules.height_rules: For Wales Part 6 agricultural development, a building should not exceed 12 metres in height, or 3 metres if within 3 kilometres of an aerodrome.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth rule. What matters is the footprint, operational need and whether the proposal stays within Part 6 limits rather than becoming a larger barn or industrial-style building needing full permission.
rules.boundary_rules: A building should not be within 25 metres of a trunk or classified road. Buildings for livestock, slurry or sewage sludge also face separation limits from protected buildings, and access works may require their own prior notification.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate roof right beyond the overall size and prior approval process. Roof pitch, ridge height and projection are judged through the permitted development limits and, where required, appearance and siting approval.
rules.materials_rules: Appearance and siting can be reserved for prior approval. Use practical agricultural materials and colours that reduce glare and visual impact, especially on exposed sites.

On exposed coastal farmland, colours, roof reflectivity and sheltering from wider views are often particularly important.

rules.height_rules: In Blaenau Gwent, the 12m figure may be the legal ceiling for many Part 6 schemes, but the real test is whether ridge and eaves height are genuinely proportionate to the holding and its setting.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth rule. What matters is the footprint, operational need and whether the proposal stays within Part 6 limits rather than becoming a larger barn or industrial-style building needing full permission.
rules.boundary_rules: A building should not be within 25 metres of a trunk or classified road. Buildings for livestock, slurry or sewage sludge also face separation limits from protected buildings, and access works may require their own prior notification. On exposed coastal farmland, colours, roof reflectivity and sheltering from wider views are often particularly important.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate roof right beyond the overall size and prior approval process. Roof pitch, ridge height and projection are judged through the permitted development limits and, where required, appearance and siting approval.
rules.materials_rules: Appearance and siting can be reserved for prior approval. Use practical agricultural materials and colours that reduce glare and visual impact, especially on exposed sites. On exposed coastal farmland, colours, roof reflectivity and sheltering from wider views are often particularly important.

restrictions.conservation_area: Agricultural development in or near a conservation area may face closer scrutiny on siting, scale and materials, even where Part 6 rights are available.
restrictions.listed_building: Works to or affecting a listed building or its curtilage can need listed building consent as well as any planning approval.

rules.permitted_development: In Wales, Part 6 rights for agricultural buildings apply only on a qualifying agricultural unit and only for genuinely agricultural purposes. In authorities with more urban-edge land, that is often the first hurdle: paddocks, storage yards, mixed commercial land or hobby use will not automatically benefit, even before size and prior approval rules are considered.

rules.height_rules: In Torfaen, the 12m figure may be the legal ceiling for many Part 6 schemes, but the real test is whether ridge and eaves height are genuinely proportionate to the holding and its setting.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth rule. What matters is whether the footprint and scale are genuinely required for agriculture and stay within Part 6 limits rather than creating a larger non-agricultural shed needing full permission.
rules.boundary_rules: A building should not be within 25 metres of a trunk or classified road. Access works, changes of level and evidence that the land is part of a real agricultural unit are often checked carefully on urban-edge sites.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate roof right beyond the overall size and prior approval process. Ridge form, roof pitch and bulk can still be examined through siting and appearance approval.
rules.materials_rules: Appearance and siting can be reserved for prior approval. Practical agricultural materials are expected, but colours and finishes should still reduce visual impact, especially near settlements.

rules.permitted_development: On a qualifying agricultural unit in Wales, certain agricultural buildings can be permitted development under Part 6, but in a national park the siting, visual effect and operational justification are likely to be examined closely. Prior notification or prior approval is commonly needed before work starts.

rules.height_rules: In Bannau Brycheiniog National Park, height is usually judged through landform and public views as much as through the numeric Part 6 ceiling, so a lower and simpler roof form is often the safer approach.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth rule. The important questions are footprint, operational need and whether the building stays proportionate to the holding and the landscape setting.
rules.boundary_rules: A building should not be within 25 metres of a trunk or classified road. Access works, cut-and-fill and new hardstandings can be just as important as the barn itself in a protected landscape.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate roof right. Roof bulk, pitch and profile are controlled through the overall Part 6 limits and can still be reviewed through prior approval of siting and appearance.
rules.materials_rules: Use practical agricultural materials and subdued colours. Bright cladding, reflective roofs and prominent siting are more likely to attract objection in a protected landscape.
